nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaches the kelp canopy and drives growth of algae, plankton and island plants.

nodes.name: Cool nutrient-rich water
nodes.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water from the deep ocean feeds the plankton and kelp around the islands.

nodes.name: Winter rain
nodes.desc: Most rain on the islands falls in the cooler months, which sets the growing season for scrub and wildflowers.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead kelp, carcasses and plant litter and return nutrients to the water and soil.

nodes.name: Giant kelp
nodes.desc: Forms tall underwater forests off the islands that shelter and feed many animals. Urchins graze it.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae at the base of the open-water food web, grazed by zooplankton and small fish.

nodes.name: California sagebrush
nodes.desc: A common shrub of the coastal scrub on the islands; its flowers and seeds feed insects and small animals.

nodes.name: Lemonade berry
nodes.desc: An evergreen shrub of island scrub and canyons with flowers visited by insects.

nodes.name: Purple sea urchin
nodes.desc: A grazer of kelp. When its predators are scarce it can overgraze kelp forests.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny grazers of phytoplankton that feed small schooling fish.

nodes.name: Vosnesensky Bumble Bee
nodes.desc: A bumble bee recorded often on the islands; it feeds on nectar and pollen of scrub flowers.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small omnivore of island scrub, eating seeds and insects. Island foxes eat it, according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: California sheephead
nodes.desc: A reef fish that eats sea urchins, crabs and molluscs. Wikipedia calls it a keystone predator of urchins in southern California.

nodes.name: Northern anchovy
nodes.desc: A schooling fish that eats plankton and is a main food for sea lions and seabirds.

nodes.name: Brown pelican
nodes.desc: A plunge-diving seabird that eats schooling fish. Seabirds were hit hard by the 1969 oil spill nearby.

nodes.name: California sea lion
nodes.desc: A sea lion that breeds and feeds around the islands and eats schooling fish.

nodes.name: Western gull
nodes.desc: A gull that breeds on the islands and feeds on fish and scavenged carcasses; GloBI records it eating sea lion and seal.

nodes.name: Island fox
nodes.desc: A small fox found only on the islands. It eats fruit, insects, lizards, birds and deer mice.

nodes.name: Island fence lizard
nodes.desc: A lizard of the islands that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Island foxes eat lizards.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: A top ocean predator recorded in the channel; GloBI shows it eating sea lions and seals.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Colonised the islands in the 1990s and preyed heavily on island foxes, which crashed in number. Eagles were later trapped and moved.
